Alternatively, solve for one radius at a time, fixing the others, and cycle through them to find a valid packing with large radii.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Growth

backlog.spec: Modify the SLSQP objective function to include a penalty term for overlapping circles and boundary violations, rather than using hard constraints. This allows the solver to traverse infeasible regions (where circles overlap) to reach better local optima. After the solver finishes its iterations, run the existing _repair function to project the result back into the feasible space.
backlog.title: Soft Penalty Objective with Hard Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed 80% time fraction for random restarts, implement an adaptive approach. If a restart produces a significantly better sum of radii (e.g., > 1% improvement), grant the next solve attempt more iterations (MAX_ITER) or more time. If the solver is struggling (no improvement for 3 restarts), reduce the time spent on the current unsuccessful branch.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit per Restart

backlog.spec: After the SLSQP solver returns a result and the repair step is complete, implement a simple local search: randomly select a circle, slightly perturb its center (within a small epsilon), and check if the sum of radii can be increased by slightly expanding its radius without causing overlaps. Repeat this for a fixed number of iterations or until the time limit is nearly reached.
backlog.title: Local Search Post-processing

backlog.spec: To speed up the constraint evaluations in SLSQP, pre-calculate the distances between all pairs of centers at the start of each _solve_once call. While the centers change, this can be used to optimize the construction of the Jacobian if using a method that supports it, or at least to quickly identify which constraints are currently violated during the repair step.
backlog.title: Pre-calculate Distance Matrix

backlog.spec: Change the objective function from maximizing the sum of radii $\sum r_i$ to maximizing a weighted sum $\sum w_i r_i$ where $w_i$ is inversely proportional to the radius. This encourages the optimizer to find a balanced distribution of circle sizes, preventing the solver from simply making a few large circles and ignoring many small ones, which might lead to a higher total sum in the long run.
backlog.title: Normalized Radius Sum

backlog.spec: Modify the _repair function to include a 'jitter' component. When shrinking radii to resolve an overlap between circle $i$ and $j$, instead of a deterministic shrinkage, add a small amount of random noise to the shrinkage factor. Run the repair loop multiple times per solve to explore different ways of resolving the same overlap, keeping the best result.
backlog.title: Jittered Repair

backlog.spec: Instead of the standard $c_i /less / than / 1 - r_i$ constraints, use a slightly stricter constraint like $c_i /less / than / (1 - r_i - /epsilon)$ to ensure that even with floating point inaccuracies, the circles never touch the boundary. Additionally, add a penalty for circles being too close to the corners of the unit square.
backlog.title: Refined Boundary Constraints

backlog.spec: After a successful solve, take the resulting centers and radii and add a small random perturbation (e.g., 1-2% of the side length) to the centers and a small random change to the radii. Then, run the SLSQP solver again starting from this perturbed point. Repeat this process for the remainder of the time limit to 'hop' into adjacent basins of attraction.
backlog.title: Basin Hopping Perturbation

backlog.spec: Instead of uniform small radii, initialize the radii such that the sum of their areas $\sum \pi r_i^2$ is as close to the maximum possible packing density (around 0.8) as possible, while keeping the radii distributed across different scales (some very small, some medium). This provides a much more 'full' starting state for the optimizer than a tiny initial radius.
backlog.title: Area-Proportional Initialization

backlog.spec: Instead of initializing all radii to a fixed small value, initialize all radii to 0. In the objective function, maximize the sum of radii while adding a constraint that the radii must be non-decreasing: r[i] <= r[i+1] (after sorting). Or more simply, solve for the sum of radii but use a 'growth' constraint where each radius r[i] is initialized based on its current relative size to ensure the solver doesn't zero out small circles too quickly.
backlog.title: Sequential Radius Growth

backlog.spec: Instead of a fixed time slice for each _solve_once, implement a dynamic budget. For the first few iterations, give the solver 10 seconds. If the objective improves significantly, increase the budget for the next call. If the improvement stalls, reduce the budget to quickly sample new starting points. This prevents 'getting stuck' on a local optimum while allowing deep exploration of good areas.
backlog.title: Adaptive Time Limit per Restart

backlog.spec: In the _repair function, after calculating the shrinkage factor 's' for the most overlapping circles, apply a small random jitter (e.g., 0.99 to 1.005) to the shrinkage factor before updating r[i] and r[j]. This helps the repair step avoid 'oscillating' between two different overlap states and can find a more relaxed local configuration.
backlog.title: Jittered Repair

backlog.spec: Replace the simple boundary constraints (c[:, 0] - r, etc.) with a more robust formulation that ensures a minimum buffer. Instead of just 0 and 1, use epsilon-margins (e.g., 1e-9) to ensure that even after floating point errors in the solver, the repair step doesn't have to shrink the radii to zero to meet the harness's 1e-10 tolerance.
backlog.title: Refined Boundary Constraints

backlog.spec: After _solve_once and _repair, implement a local expansion step. Identify circles that are not touching any other circle and are not touching the boundary. For these circles, try to incrementally increase their radii by a small amount (e.g., 0.001) until they hit an obstacle. Repeat this for all circles until no further expansion is possible. This polishes the packing found by SLSQP.
backlog.title: Local Search: Expansion Step

backlog.spec: Maintain the 'best' packing found so far. In each iteration of the while loop, there is a 30% chance to start a new solve from a random initialization and a 70% chance to start from a slightly perturbed version of the current 'best' packing (e.g., move centers by 0.01 and radii by 0.005). Run SLSQP on this perturbed version to 'hop' to a neighboring basin.
backlog.title: Multi-start Refinement (Basin Hopping Style)

backlog.spec: In the objective function, use the sum of (radii^2) as the primary objective but keep the return value as the sum of radii. This makes the solver favor larger circles (which contribute more to area) more strongly, but the harness still evaluates the sum of radii. This can be adjusted by using a weighted sum: sum(radii^p) where p is between 1.0 and 2.0.
backlog.title: Area-Proportional Weighting

backlog.spec: In the objective function, instead of just the sum of radii, add a small regularization term that penalizes circles being too close to each other (e.g., sum(max(0, r_i + r_j - dist_ij)^2)). This creates a 'force field' that helps the SLSQP solver stay away from the hard boundaries of the overlap constraints, leading to smoother convergence.
backlog.title: Pre-calculated Distance Matrix with Regularization
